evidence.field: 甲骨文释形与卜辞用例；商代“受年”义
evidence.text: The museum identifies 年 in oracle bone inscriptions as a harvest term, explaining its visible structure as 禾 above 人 and citing an actual divination pair, “我受年 / 我不其受年,” asking whether there would be a good harvest. This supports an early harvest sense and the depicted person-with-grain interpretation; it does not establish that 人 was a phonetic component.
evidence.kind: primary institutional paleographic account with transcribed inscription
evidence.title: 我受年──甲骨文「年」的故事

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Center for Digital Cultures / Chinese Character Database
evidence.text: The entry assigns 年 the basic meaning “harvest,” describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as 禾 above 人, and says the small-seal form’s lower 人 changed erroneously into 千. Its displayed chronology includes oracle-bone, bronze, Chu manuscript, small-seal and 說文 categories. The detailed shapes are presented as images; those images were not inspected here.
evidence.title: 漢字「年」：字形演變

evidence.field: 甲骨文语义用例；字形、读音分析之分歧；“年/歲/祀”用法
evidence.text: The article discusses an oracle-bone example from the late Shang fifth period, dated in its account to the Di Yi/Di Xin period, containing 年、歲、祀. It interprets 年 as harvest/yield, 歲 as harvest season, and 祀 as the regnal-year count in “王八祀.” It says 周 usage later replaces 祀 with 年 for regnal dating. The article also reports the Shuowen analysis “年，穀熟也。从禾，千聲,” while its own oracle-bone analysis treats 禾 as semantic and 人 as a phonetic element (read ジン). These phonetic claims conflict with the depicted-person interpretation and require phonological evaluation; the article supplies no reconstruction in the inspected text. The dated text locates the example within a Shang period, but no absolute year is supplied.
evidence.title: 漢字の来た道｜漢字文化資料館

gaps: The inspected evidence supports an early harvest sense and attested Shang “受年” use, but it does not establish a complete dated semantic pathway from harvest to annual period, calendar year, New Year, or a person’s age. The Taishukan example supports a distinction among 年、歲、祀 in a particular Shang inscription and its account reports later Zhou replacement of 祀 by 年 in regnal dating; broader chronology remains unestablished here.

The Academia Sinica material supports 禾 plus a lower human-shaped element as a pictorial interpretation. Whether 人 also functioned phonologically in the earliest form is disputed in the inspected sources: Taishukan proposes a sound role, while the museum describes a person carrying grain and does not establish phonetic function. No sufficient reconstruction or primary phonetic-series evidence was inspected to settle this.

The later lower 千 and Shuowen’s “从禾千声” analysis are documented as a graphic/dictionary account; the claim that 千 arose through corruption of 人 is asserted by the Academia Sinica database, but no inspected glyph images or independently dated forms were examined here.

Exact local and official Unihan kMandarin verification is incomplete: local row 年 = nián was supplied, while Unicode’s exact U+5E74 record URL was inaccessible. The exact local Baxter–Sagart row is likewise input provenance rather than externally inspected evidence. No component character is established as a phonetic component, so no component sound array is offered.
No evidence in the inspected sources establishes the sound or independent name of a depicted object as a basis for whole-graph borrowing; no whole-graph loan hypothesis is advanced.
